mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕“艺术”话题，涵盖走进美术馆（Reading：奥赛博物馆与印象派）、传世名画《清明上河图》（Extended reading）和艺术与学校生活（Integrated skills）三个子话题——艺术鉴赏与文化传播是高考应用文的高频场景，也是雅思艺术教育类议论文的核心命题。

subTopics.title: 走进美术馆
subTopics.desc: 课文游记：在奥赛博物馆 lay eyes on the real thing——nothing could have prepared me for the wonder I felt。

prompts.task: 你校英文报“艺术之窗”栏目征稿。请你写一篇短文，记述你参观一次画展（或美术馆）的经历，内容包括：1. 参观概况；2. 印象最深的一幅作品及原因；3. 你的收获。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Standing Before the Real Thing

Last month I visited the provincial art museum with my classmates.

Even though I had admired the famous painting hundreds of times on my phone screen, nothing could have prepared me for the wonder I felt when I finally laid eyes on the real thing. Seen up close, the small areas of light across the canvas seemed alive, and the way the soft edges of the figures mixed together was something no screen could show.

Although the works had very different styles, it was their power to slow me down that stayed with me long after I left. In an age of two-second swipes, a museum teaches us the oldest skill: to stand still and truly see.
vocabHints: lay eyes on the real thing
nothing could have prepared me for

prompts.task: Some people think that art galleries and museums are no longer necessary because people can see artworks online. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Now that every masterpiece is a search away, some conclude that the buildings which house the originals have outlived their purpose. I disagree with this view almost entirely: the screen has changed how we preview art, not how we experience it.

The case for the online view deserves fair statement. Digital galleries have democratised access on a scale museums never approached — a student in a small town can study distant collections nightly, zooming into brushwork invisible from behind a rope. For education, comparison and simple awareness, the screen is a gift, and museums themselves know it: their best websites are their longest arms.

Yet seeing an image is not standing before a painting, and the difference is the museum's whole argument. Scale vanishes on a phone: a canvas that fills a wall and a miniature arrive as the same rectangle. Texture vanishes too — the ridges of paint, the light that shifts as the viewer moves — and with them goes the strange authority of the original, the knowledge that this very object left the artist's hands. Museums also curate an experience screens cannot: silence, sequence and the discipline of standing still, in which attention deepens from a glance into an encounter. It is telling that decades of perfect reproductions have not emptied galleries but filled them — the preview feeds the pilgrimage.

My conclusion is that screens and galleries have settled into partnership: one distributes images, the other guards presence. A civilisation that kept only the copies would soon forget what all the copies are copies of.

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):'The case for the online view deserves fair statement'/'Yet seeing an image is not standing before a painting'/'My conclusion is...'——推进清楚;'their best websites are their longest arms'与'the preview feeds the pilgrimage'两个警句分别收束两段;'copies are copies of'的绕口令式收尾点题原作价值。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):'a search away'、'outlived their purpose'、'zooming into brushwork invisible from behind a rope'、'the strange authority of the original'、'from a glance into an encounter'、'guards presence'——原创密集;课文体验(nothing could have prepared me/up close)转写为论证机制。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):now that 开篇、破折号插入、it is telling that 强调、条件虚拟收尾('A civilisation that kept only the copies would...');复杂句准确。

subTopics.title: 传世名画：清明上河图
subTopics.desc: 课文赏析：hundreds of people from all walks of life 尽入画卷——displays a remarkable mastery of perspective 的国宝长卷。

prompts.task: 你的法国笔友 Marie 正在做“世界名画”课题，来信请你介绍一幅中国名画。请你写一封回信介绍《清明上河图》，内容包括：1. 画作基本信息；2. 画面内容与艺术特色；3. 观看建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Marie,

For your project, let me introduce Riverside Scene at Qingming, one of China's most treasured paintings.

It is commonly believed that the city described in the painting is Bianjing, capital of the Northern Song Dynasty about 900 years ago. Along the five-metre scroll, hundreds of people from all walks of life — butchers, hairdressers, boatmen and officials — can be seen going about their daily business. Using ink on silk, the artist Zhang Zeduan created amazingly realistic images and displayed a remarkable mastery of perspective.

My advice: don't try to see it all at once. View it slowly from right to left, like unrolling a movie of ancient China, and the busy river city will come alive before your eyes.

Yours,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people believe that a country's art and cultural treasures are the best way for foreigners to understand that country. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Nations introduce themselves in many ways — through trade, tourism and news — but some hold that art and cultural treasures make the deepest ambassadors. I agree to a large extent: art carries what official channels cannot, though it serves understanding best as an entrance rather than a summary.

The strengths of art as national introduction are considerable. First, art is testimony without argument: a thousand-year-old scroll crowded with boatmen, pedlars and officials shows a civilisation's daily life with a candour no brochure would risk, and viewers trust what was never designed to persuade them. Second, art travels across language as facts cannot: a foreigner may forget every date of a dynasty yet remember forever the bustle of a painted river city, because images lodge where statistics slide off. Third, treasures embody values silently — what a culture chose to paint, preserve and perfect reveals what it loved.

The reservation, however, is real. Treasures are a country's edited highlights: masterpieces record the tastes of courts and collectors more often than the lives of the poor, and the distance between a golden age on silk and a modern nation on smartphones can mislead the viewer who mistakes heritage for description. Art opens the door in the warmest way; but a door is an invitation, not a tour.

My conclusion is that cultural treasures are the best beginning of understanding and a poor substitute for the rest of it. Let the scroll enchant first — then let the visitor board a real bus, in the real city, where the boatmen's descendants live now.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):程度表态精确('to a large extent + entrance rather than summary'),支持段三层机制(无意说服的证词/图像跨语言的记忆优势/珍宝的价值观显影),保留段指出'精选集偏差',结论给出行动序('先让画卷迷人,再上真实的公交')——层次完整。

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):'First... Second... Third...'的机制列举/'The reservation, however, is real'/'My conclusion is...'——结构显豁;'a door is an invitation, not a tour'承接选必一U3同款门喻并翻新;结尾'boatmen's descendants'回收画卷意象。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):'the deepest ambassadors'、'testimony without argument'、'a candour no brochure would risk'、'images lodge where statistics slide off'、'edited highlights'、'mistake heritage for description'——原创概念句密集;课文画卷细节(boatmen/all walks of life)匿名织入论据。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):破折号插入、because 机制句、what 从句作主语('what a culture chose to paint...reveals...')、祈使式结论;句式多样准确。
vsGaokao: 素材用法:课文清明上河图在回信中完整点名介绍;雅思中化为'a thousand-year-old scroll crowded with boatmen'的匿名论据——同一幅画,导览vs证据。
体裁:回信是名画介绍(信息+特色+建议);雅思论'艺术能否代表国家'。
语域:回信有'like unrolling a movie'的生动导览;雅思以'real bus, real city'的落地收束。
评分维度:雅思看'入口而非总结'的边界论证;高考看信息准确、介绍生动、建议贴心。

subTopics.title: 一幅让我惊叹的画
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：gaze in wonder at、be bathed in light、light and shade、be reduced to tears——好的画作会让人 wonder at 它的光影，甚至久久说不出话。

prompts.task: 你校英文报征集 "A Work of Art That Moved Me" 主题稿件。请你写一篇短文，介绍一幅让你惊叹的画作，内容包括：1. 画作简介；2. 它打动你的地方。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Last month, on a school trip to the art museum, I stood before a painting that I will never forget.

It showed a small figure walking home at dusk, the whole valley bathed in the last golden light. What amazed me was its handling of light and shade: the darkness of the hills made the glowing sky feel almost alive. I gazed at it in wonder, and for a moment the noisy gallery seemed to fall silent.

I am not an artist, and I cannot fully explain why, but I was very nearly reduced to tears. A great painting does not simply show us the world; it makes us see it as if for the first time. That, I think, is the quiet power of art.
vocabHints: bathed in the last golden light
its handling of light and shade
made the glowing sky feel alive

prompts.task: Some people think that governments should spend public money supporting art such as painting and music, while others believe this money should be spent on more practical things. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Whenever budgets are debated, spending on painting, music and museums competes with roads, hospitals and schools. Some see public funding of the arts as an indulgence; others regard it as essential to a civilised society. Having weighed both views, I believe governments should continue to support the arts, though never at the expense of basic human needs.

Those who resist arts funding argue from priority. When people lack housing or medical care, spending tax money on galleries can seem hard to justify, and they add that art should survive on its own merits, funded by those who actually enjoy it rather than by every taxpayer.

The opposing case, which I find stronger, rests on value that markets alone cannot secure. Art records a nation's history and identity, enriches education, and gives life meaning beyond mere survival; a country that feeds the body while starving the imagination is poorer for it. Public funding also keeps culture open to everyone, not just those wealthy enough to pay, and the arts repay investment concretely — museums and music draw tourism, employ thousands and revive whole city districts. Left entirely to the market, much serious and experimental work, unable to turn an immediate profit, would simply disappear.

The reasonable path is proportion. Essential services must come first, but the modest sums the arts require — often a tiny fraction of public spending — yield cultural and economic returns out of all proportion to their cost.

In conclusion, while practical needs rightly take priority, governments should still fund the arts, because a society that values only the useful ends up impoverished in every sense that matters.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点均展开(反对方:民生优先/自负盈亏;支持方:历史身份/普惠/旅游回报/市场失灵)，立场'继续资助但不越过基本需求'权重清晰，结论落到'比例'。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):Those who resist / The opposing case, which I find stronger / The reasonable path / In conclusion 推进工整;'feeds the body while starving the imagination'点睛并在结尾呼应。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):an indulgence / survive on its own merits / out of all proportion to their cost / impoverished in every sense 表达精准。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):which非限定从句表评价、Left entirely分词条件、破折号插入、because收尾推理，句式多样。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考写打动我的画作短文(简介+原因);雅思写公共艺术资助双边议论文。
论据来源:高考短文织入课件'bathed in light / light and shade / gaze in wonder / reduced to tears'词块;雅思用文化政策的普适论据(市场失灵)。
语域:短文有个人惊叹(fall silent);雅思客观权衡，'比例'立场显层次。
评分维度:高考重共鸣+要点;雅思discuss题高分在于第三方案——'比例而非取舍'超越二元。

prompts.task: 你校艺术节将举办“创意工坊”（Creative Workshop）活动，面向全体学生开放。请你以组委会名义写一则英文通知，内容包括：1. 活动内容（如蔬果拼贴肖像、旧物改造等）；2. 时间地点与报名方式；3. 欢迎参加。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Notice

Think art belongs only to galleries? Come to our Creative Workshop at this year's Art Festival and think again!

At the workshop, you can arrange fruits and vegetables on toast to create your own portrait, turn old bottles into flower vases, and paint pebbles into pandas. No drawing skills are required — what matters is imagination, not technique. All materials will be provided free.

Time: 2–5 p.m., this Friday
Place: Art Building, Room 101
Sign-up: scan the QR code on the poster before Thursday

Come and discover the artist hidden in you. Everyone is welcome!

The Organising Committee

prompts.task: Some people think that art and music classes are less important than academic subjects such as maths and science, and should be optional in schools. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In timetables crowded with examinations, art and music are usually the first classes surrendered, on the theory that they decorate an education rather than constitute one. I disagree with this view almost completely: the arts train capacities that academic subjects assume but never teach, and making them optional guarantees that the students who need them most will never choose them.

The argument for demotion sounds hard-headed. Mathematics and science open careers and feed economies; parents and governments, paying for measurable outcomes, reasonably prioritise subjects with answer keys. Class time is finite, and in the arithmetic of timetabling, a drawing lesson competes directly with exam marks that decide futures.

Yet this accounting misses what the arts uniquely supply. They are the only school subjects where there is no single right answer, and thus the only regular training in judgement — in making choices that must be defended by taste and intention rather than formula. They teach the tolerance of early failure that every creative profession, including science itself, runs on: a child who reworks a painting learns revision more deeply than one who checks answers. Studies of learning repeatedly find that arts education strengthens the very attention and confidence that academic subjects then harvest. The scientist who imagines a new experiment is using a muscle first exercised, in most lives, with crayons.

My conclusion is that the hierarchy is false and self-defeating. Arts classes are not a rest from serious learning; they are where several serious things are learned for the first time. Schools should keep them compulsory — not as decoration, but as foundation.
